Keep patch evidence together.

Terminal output disappears. Agent narration changes. The ledger keeps files, commands, tests, and delegated tasks together.

How it works

Create a review ledger in three steps.

Any agent, hook, shell, or CI job can write documented JSONL events.

  1. 01
    { }

    Record JSONL events

    Write one strict event for a file, command, test, or delegated task. Unknown fields fail loudly.

  2. 02
    ⌁

    Hash and connect

    The CLI hashes current files and artifacts, then links execution evidence to each change.

  3. 03
    ✓

    Export and verify

    Hand reviewers clean Markdown plus structured JSON. Add an Ed25519 signature when provenance matters.

Browser workbench

Build a review ledger in your browser.

Paste JSONL below. The workbench processes it locally and does not upload it.

Action events

One JSON object per line. Prompts and file contents are not accepted fields.

A unique file name also matches a directory-qualified event path such as src/lib.rs.

CLI usage

Build a review ledger from the command line.

Run it beside any coding agent. It needs no account or running service.

shell
$ cargo install agent-audit-ledger

$ aal demo
✓ Demo ledger written to a new temporary directory

$ aal build --input actions.jsonl \
    --markdown audit.md --json audit.json --root .

✓ 4 files · 7 evidence events · paths redacted
  • One binaryRuns in a shell
  • Two exportsMarkdown + strict JSON
  • Bundled sampleaal demo writes only to a new temp folder
